page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the system features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 380,524.27 and a PassMark CPU score of 107,915.98. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 725.79 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 330.7 GB/sec for large-block write operations. The server demonstrates strong cryptographic capabilities with a PassMark encryption score of 56,832.22, supported by hardware-level AES. Single-threaded performance is moderate, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,013.79.

This server is optimized for highly parallelized workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. It achieves 520.51 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 355.34 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. While prompt processing for small and medium language models is highly efficient, text generation speeds are limited, averaging 15.85 tokens/sec on a 7B model due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The combination of massive local NVMe storage and high memory bandwidth makes it suitable for large-scale databases, containerized microservices, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server featuring 192 dedicated physical cores of AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Lacking a GPU, the server relies on its high-density ARM architecture to deliver top-tier multi-core performance, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 107,915.98 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1,953.03 GB/sec. It excels in memory bandwidth and database operations, achieving 520.51 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. This configuration is highly suitable for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and parallel data processing, though it exhibits lower performance in single-threaded tasks and LLM text generation.
